profile.headline: Software Engineer at PayPal
profile.summary:
I'm a full-stack JavaScript developer currently working as a Frontend Software Engineer for PayPal.

I have a keen interest in JavaScript development, particularly with Node.js and front-end frameworks like React and AngularJS. I've also delved into Python and iOS/Swift. I have experience of the following languages and technologies, amongst others:

▪ Platforms: JavaScript/Node.js, Typescript, Python, Swift, Web and Mobile-Web (HTML5/CSS3)
▪ Frameworks: React.js, Next.js, AngularJS, Ember, Polymer, Flask
▪ Libraries: Formik, Jest, Nightwatch.js, Recharts, Nivo, Bootstrap, Materialize, Socket.IO, Mocha, Chai
▪ Servers: Express.js, Linux, NGINX
▪ Databases: MySQL, MongoDB/Mongoose
▪ Other Technologies: React Native, Xcode, Git/GitHub

Before making a career change to programming, I completed a 4-year integrated MRes/PhD studentship funded by Newcastle University, which I graduated from in July 2016. My PhD research was in the field of Molecular Microbiology, and aimed at investigating the effect and role of the amino acid L-arginine on Streptococcus gordonii biofilms, particularly the impact it can have on gene expression and biofilm formation itself. I was supervised by Dr Nick Jakubovics and Dr Matthew German of the School of Dental Sciences, and Prof Waldemar Vollmer of the Centre for Bacterial Cell Biology.

If you'd like to contact me, please email me at: contact@jillcrobinson.com
Github: https://github.com/wildlingjill
Website: jillcrobinson.com
YouTube: youtube.jillcrobinson.com

positions.title: Undergraduate Laboratory Assistant
positions.description: During my BSc studies, I worked as a part-time laboratory assistant for a year in a Newcastle University research lab. This involved preparing equipment and solutions for experimental work by research associates, and occasionally assisting in experiments such as PCR, gel extraction and gel electrophoresis.

volunteerExperiences.description: Welcomed prospective students as they arrived for the visit day. Assisted them in finding lecture theatres for talk sessions, local amenities etc.

Helped to run an event at the British Science Festival (from the Oral Biology lab at Newcastle University), named "What's Hiding in Your Mouth?", aimed primarily at educating children about microbiology, immunology and oral health. Answered questions, helped to stain cheek swabs for microscopy and with plaque disclosing staining. Organised a (popular!) competition for the children to win prizes.
